applies_why: The judge text resolves the Luke 2:48-49 collision by an immediate phrase-to-phrase qualification, which is the kind of verse-level treatment K-C governs.
quote: Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" / "weighs chain against chain by footing": whether immediate qualification inside Luke 2:48-49 can decide the collision or whether the judge must weigh the competing chains' footing; I read the rule as requiring chain-by-chain footing.
why: The judge resolves the collision by saying one phrase in the passage is immediately qualified by another, rather than weighing the pressing chain against the link by footing as K-C requires.
